correctness.rationale: For unnormalized surface measure on S², exact Fourier--Bessel decomposition gives N(f)^4=(2pi)^6 sum_{k,l} a_k a_l M_{kl} with a_k=||P_k f||² and M_{kl}=integral J_{k+1/2}² J_{l+1/2}². Legendre self-convolution, Fourier inversion and Plancherel show M_{0k}=1/[pi(2k+1)] for every k>=0. Independently integrated F1’(x)²/2 over [0,2] to get pi M11=7/15. Xu arXiv:2610.19648 Theorem1.2 proves strict M00>M11>M22>... for d=3,q=4. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds every k,l>=1 by M11, strictly when any k>=2; collecting a0=(1-b)A gives (2pi)^6/pi*(1-4b/3+4b²/5)A². Equality iff only modes k=0,1; b endpoints and complex amplitudes covered. General theorem relies on Xu infinite-mode ordering, not finite CHECK.py.

Xu’s Minkowski-based squared-norm estimate has cross coefficient sqrt(7/15), larger than exact new 1/3; its square is strictly weaker for 0<b<1. The exact constant-to-any-mode integral and sharp fixed-b quartic are not in the inspected relevant source sections. Historical equivalent nonlinear stability refinements may exist.
